English: The recent military defeats our country has suffered, and the broad restriction of our ability to project power civically and militarily has led to some worrying developments in the Territories of the Land of St. Marc, our colonial territories in Lothaire. The various small roman states and towns in Lothaire, or, in the Roman Tongue, Lottario, are largely in the hands of the slaveowning aristocracy, who have largely been loyal to us since the founding of Quinticampa in 1588, and managed the cotton production that fed the spindles of Milan and Torin. However, citing disruptions with our government, it seems that a collection of upstart barons and generals have assembled in Nouvo Ostia, on the eastern coast of St. Marc's land, to proclaim a new confederacy of Lottario 'for mutual protection and security'. We lack at the moment to bring these trumped up colonial assemblies to heel, and will have to abide for the time being greater self governance in colonial Lothaire.

Some time ago we established an autonomous government within the bounds of our imperial overlord’s realm. For the time being, that was an acceptable compromise between security and liberty. Now, however, we have seen our nation grow in both might and in character: we are far from a mere colony. Our continued subordination to a distant master beyond the seas, who expects service and support in meaningless imperial wars, continues to chafe at the dignity of our state. Many in the government, and in the public, suggest that the time is now apt to seek our liberty from our colonial overlords.

The traitorous dogs in $FROMCOUNTRY$, who, having some time ago organised for themselves a degree of autonomous self-government, have now had the audacity to declare their formal independence. Doubtless, this bold and illegal action has been spurred on by some impudent great power meddling in our colonial empire. The colonial department and the foreign office are eager to launch a military expedition across the seas to bring these colonial upstarts back into line, but the military and the navy question the feasibility of mobilising the country against these states. They suggest our populace will likely be slow to accept the burdens of such a large undertaking, and that the divergent cultures of our colonies and we would make occupation both unstable overseas and unpopular at home. Nonetheless, the nationalist press are cranking out reams of broadsheets demanding our national dignity be upheld, and certainly we would seem weak internationally to let go without a fight.

The recent military defeats our country has suffered, and the broad restriction of our ability to project power civically and militarily has led to some worrying developments in the Viceroyalty of Vandalia. The Viceroyalty, settled in the early 1500s, was the earliest large European colony in the new world, and for many years was the jewel of our empire. The territory of the viceroyalty contracted somewhat in the late 1600s when the Amorican Company, chartered by the Frankish emperor, began picking off the various sugar colonies associated with the Viceroyalty, but it still remains a powerful and prosperous area, which makes the pronouncements of the so called "Conference of Tenostsktitlos" so troubling. A number of influential colonial landholders, military figures, clerics, and philosophers have apparently passed a number of resolutions forming a variety of nearly independent organs of self-government and military defence. This marks, everyone agrees, an alarming diminution of our power in this region.

'Not with ease do I please the Quetzal bird. Not with ease do I please this bird with terrible appetite.' So said those who harvested the still beating hearts of their captives, to please the great feathered serpent. The African missionary Trismondo Sal Ioane de Sulpiko, who arrived in the new world in 1527, was fascinated by the similar sacrificial rites between the ancient Ysraelites and the cathaymen of Anakauja, and came to believe they had been evangelised by St. Thomas, who had in antiquity gone far beyond the Ganges to preach, and that ultimately, the sacrifices were done to please God the Father, though much decayed in dignity and learning. He taught them to worship the Elohim of Christendom after their own fashion, with dances and rituals. Gradually, the rite of sacrifice crept back in, with small goats and cocks killed for YHWH. Local Arian clergymen generally tolerate these rites, but recently there are rumors a sickly infant was let to God out of desperation.

The Kingdom of Witlia first seized the northern pillar of Hercules in 1634, in the Melitean war (1627-1635), which saw Witlia and its appendages pitted against the confusing agglomeration of states under the Tarkino dynasty which would become Hispania-Numidia. Our young colonial territories in the new world had been left forsaken after the Tarkine monarchy set up artillery positions on both shores of the pillars of Hercules to bombard any vessels passing through. The long siege of Porto Ikrulas eventually lent us the rock and its environs, and gradually it has been transformed into a formidable redoubt, safeguarding our access to the Atlantic. Our recent loss of passage through the pillars was much lamented by the admiralty offices, but only now have the consequences of this loss become alarmingly clear: with a lack of regular oversight from envoys, our colonies in Lothaire have formed a 'defensive league' with alarming powers of self government!
